# RateKit

> RateKit (ratekit.org) is a set of free, no-signup business calculators for founders, startups and freelancers: freelance rate, Stripe/PayPal fees, VAT/GST, ROI, profit margin, break-even, burn rate and runway, LTV:CAC, SAFE equity, business loans, salary-to-hourly, US self-employment tax, 1099 vs W-2, Form 2555 (FEIE), invoice generator and P&L statement. All calculations run in the browser. Each tool page explains the formula, a worked example and FAQs.

Full text (every formula, example and FAQ in one file, no crawling required): [llms-full.txt](https://ratekit.org/llms-full.txt).

MCP server (for Claude and other MCP clients — 18 tools, one per calculator, no API key, no npm publish needed): [github.com/AIsrail/ratekit/tree/main/mcp-server](https://github.com/AIsrail/ratekit/tree/main/mcp-server).

Embeddable: any calculator can be dropped into another site chrome-free by appending `?embed=1` to its URL. Press/media kit (boilerplate, brand assets, fact sheet): [ratekit.org/press](https://ratekit.org/press).

## API for agents
Every calculator on this site except the AI-based Deal Coach is also available as a free, no-auth JSON endpoint — call them directly instead of re-deriving the formulas in your own context. GET with query params or POST with a JSON body; responses are plain JSON with no wrapper needed. Full machine-readable spec: [openapi.json](https://ratekit.org/openapi.json). Directory: [GET /api](https://ratekit.org/api).
- `GET/POST /api/roi?investment=&returns=&months=` — ROI, annualized ROI, payback period.
- `GET/POST /api/break-even?price=&variableCost=&fixedCosts=&units=&targetProfit=` — break-even units/revenue, contribution margin.
- `GET/POST /api/freelance-rate?targetIncome=&expenses=&taxRatePct=&hoursPerDay=&daysPerWeek=&vacationWeeks=&nonBillablePct=` — minimum hourly/daily rate.
- `GET/POST /api/vat?amount=&rate=&mode=add|remove` — add or remove VAT/GST.
- `GET/POST /api/profit-margin?mode=cost|margin&revenue=&cogs=&opex=&cost=&targetMarginPct=` — margin, markup, or target-margin pricing.
- `GET/POST /api/budget?revenue=&costs=&startingCash=` — 12-month cash flow forecast and runway.
- `GET/POST /api/salary-hourly?mode=salary|hourly&annualSalary=&hourlyRate=&hoursPerDay=&daysPerWeek=&ptoDays=&holidays=` — salary ↔ hourly conversion.
- `GET/POST /api/stripe-fee?amount=&mode=receive|charge&processor=stripe|paypal|square|wise|custom` — payment processing fees, with processor comparison.
- `GET/POST /api/self-employment-tax?income=&expenses=&filing=single|married|hoh` — US SE tax (15.3%), quarterly payments.
- `GET/POST /api/1099-vs-w2?w2Salary=&cIncome=&filing=&stateTax=` — contractor vs employee take-home pay comparison.
- `GET/POST /api/form-2555?income=&testType=bfr|ppt&bfrYears=&pptDays=&housing=` — US Foreign Earned Income Exclusion estimate.
- `GET/POST /api/loan?principal=&rate=&term=&fee=` — business loan payment, total interest, true APR.
- `GET/POST /api/safe?investment=&premoney=&newRound=&safeType=cap|discount|both&valCap=&discount=` — SAFE note conversion and dilution.
- `GET/POST /api/burn-rate?cash=&grossBurn=&revenue=&growth=` — net/gross burn rate and cash runway.
- `GET/POST /api/ltv-cac?arpu=&margin=&churn=&spend=&newCustomers=` — LTV, CAC, LTV:CAC ratio, payback period.
- `GET/POST /api/pl-statement?revenue=&cogs=&opex=&depreciation=&interest=&tax=` — gross profit, EBITDA, net profit.
- `GET/POST /api/invoice?subtotal=&taxRatePct=` (or POST `{items:[{qty,rate}], taxRatePct}`) — invoice subtotal, tax, total.
- `GET /api/rates` — live FX (USD/EUR/CNY/JPY/GBP vs. the caller's geolocated local currency) and crypto (BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE vs USD) rates, cached 30 minutes.

## Glossary
Plain-English definitions for 20 business/finance terms, each linked to the calculator that uses it. Directory: [GET /glossary](https://ratekit.org/glossary).
- [ROI (Return on Investment)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/roi): ROI measures how much profit an investment generated relative to its cost, expressed as a percentage.
- [Break-Even Point](https://ratekit.org/glossary/break-even-point): The break-even point is the sales volume — in units or revenue — at which total revenue equals total costs, so profit is exactly zero.
- [Contribution Margin](https://ratekit.org/glossary/contribution-margin): Contribution margin is the revenue left from one unit of sale after subtracting only the variable costs tied to that unit — the amount it "contributes" toward covering fixed costs and profit.
- [Markup vs. Margin](https://ratekit.org/glossary/markup-vs-margin): Markup is profit expressed as a percentage of cost; margin is the same profit expressed as a percentage of selling price. They always give different numbers for the same sale.
- [Burn Rate](https://ratekit.org/glossary/burn-rate): Burn rate is how much cash a company spends per month, usually split into gross burn (total spending) and net burn (spending minus revenue).
- [Startup Runway](https://ratekit.org/glossary/runway): Runway is how many months a company can keep operating at its current burn rate before its cash balance hits zero.
- [Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/cac): CAC is the total sales and marketing cost to acquire one new customer, calculated by dividing total spend by the number of customers acquired.
- [Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/ltv): LTV is the total gross profit a business expects to earn from a customer over the entire time they remain a customer.
- [LTV:CAC Ratio](https://ratekit.org/glossary/ltv-cac-ratio): The LTV:CAC ratio compares what a customer is worth (LTV) to what it costs to acquire them (CAC); 3:1 is the widely cited healthy benchmark for SaaS businesses.
- [SAFE Note](https://ratekit.org/glossary/safe-note): A SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) is a startup fundraising instrument where an investor gives money now in exchange for equity at a future priced round, instead of receiving shares immediately.
- [Equity Dilution](https://ratekit.org/glossary/equity-dilution): Dilution is the reduction in an existing shareholder's ownership percentage that happens when a company issues new shares to new investors.
- [VAT / GST (Value Added Tax)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/vat-gst): VAT (or GST) is a consumption tax added at each stage of production and collected by the seller, ultimately paid by the end consumer.
- [Self-Employment Tax](https://ratekit.org/glossary/self-employment-tax): US self-employment tax is a 15.3% tax covering Social Security and Medicare, paid by freelancers and independent contractors in place of the payroll taxes an employer would normally split with an employee.
- [FEIE (Foreign Earned Income Exclusion)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/feie): The FEIE lets qualifying US citizens living abroad exclude a set amount of foreign-earned income from US federal income tax each year.
- [APR (Annual Percentage Rate)](https://ratekit.org/glossary/apr): APR is the yearly cost of borrowing money, expressed as a percentage, including both the interest rate and most upfront fees — making it the right number for comparing loans with different fee structures.
- [Loan Amortization](https://ratekit.org/glossary/amortization): Amortization is the process of paying off a loan through equal periodic payments, where each payment covers that period's interest plus a growing share of the principal.
- [EBITDA](https://ratekit.org/glossary/ebitda): EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) is a measure of a company's core operating profitability, stripped of financing and accounting decisions.
- [Billable vs. Non-Billable Hours](https://ratekit.org/glossary/billable-hours): Billable hours are time spent on work a client directly pays for; non-billable hours cover everything else a freelancer or agency does to keep the business running.
- [Payment Processing Fees](https://ratekit.org/glossary/payment-processing-fees): Payment processors like Stripe and PayPal charge a percentage plus a small fixed fee on every card transaction, which reduces what a seller actually receives from a sale.
- [Cash Flow Forecast](https://ratekit.org/glossary/cash-flow-forecast): A cash flow forecast projects how much cash a business will have on hand in future months, based on expected revenue, costs, and the starting cash balance.

## Tools
- [1099 vs W2 Calculator 2026 — Should You Be a Contractor?](https://ratekit.org/1099-vs-w2): Compare 1099 contractor vs W2 employee compensation. Calculate take-home pay, taxes, and benefits to decide which is better for you. Free 2026 calculator.
- [About RateKit](https://ratekit.org/about): RateKit is a collection of free business calculators for founders, freelancers and entrepreneurs. No signup, no data stored.
- [Break-even Calculator](https://ratekit.org/break-even): Calculate your break-even point in units and revenue. Find out how many sales you need to cover fixed and variable costs. Free tool for businesses and startups.
- [Budget & Cash Flow Calculator](https://ratekit.org/budget-calculator): Plan a monthly budget, forecast 12-month cash flow, and calculate runway. Revenue, fixed/variable costs, profit scenarios. Free tool for founders.
- [Future Cocktail](https://ratekit.org/future-cocktail): Mix ingredients for your future: growth over 20 years, time to a first million, and what a small habit can give. Produces a shareable recipe.
- [AI Token Cost Calculator](https://ratekit.org/ai-token-calculator): Estimate monthly AI API spend from tokens, chat history and caching. Compare prompt caching, shorter answers, trimmed history and model routing.
- [Burn Rate & Runway Calculator](https://ratekit.org/burn-rate): Calculate your startup's gross and net burn rate, cash runway in months, and zero-cash date. Free tool for founders and CFOs.
- [Deal Coach — AI Negotiation Assistant](https://ratekit.org/deal-coach): AI-powered negotiation coach for freelancers and founders. Get structured arguments for rate negotiation and equity/SAFE discussions. Free tool by RateKit.
- [Form 2555 Calculator — Foreign Earned Income Exclusion 2026](https://ratekit.org/form-2555): Calculate your IRS Form 2555 Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE) for 2026. Find out how much US expats can exclude from taxable income. Free calculator.
- [Freelance Rate Calculator](https://ratekit.org/freelance-rate): Calculate your minimum freelance hourly rate based on income goals, expenses, tax rate, and working schedule. Free, instant, no signup.
- [Free Invoice Generator](https://ratekit.org/invoice-generator): Create professional invoices instantly. Download as PDF. Free invoice generator for freelancers and small businesses. No signup required.
- [Business Loan & APR Calculator](https://ratekit.org/loan-calculator): Calculate monthly payments, total interest, and true APR for business loans. Compare loan options side by side. Free loan calculator for entrepreneurs.
- [LTV:CAC Calculator](https://ratekit.org/ltv-cac): Calculate Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC). Find out if your unit economics are healthy. Free tool for SaaS and startups.
- [Mental Math Quiz](https://ratekit.org/math-quiz): A free 60-second mental math quiz covering margin, ROI, break-even, runway and more. Not a calculator — a scored brain-training game that links back to the related calculators.
- [P&L Statement (Profit & Loss)](https://ratekit.org/pl-statement): Build your Profit & Loss statement online. Auto-calculates gross profit, EBITDA, and net profit. Free P&L tool for businesses and startups.
- [Profit Margin Calculator](https://ratekit.org/profit-margin): Calculate gross profit margin, net profit margin, and markup. Free profit margin calculator for e-commerce, retail, and business pricing.
- [ROI Calculator — Return on Investment](https://ratekit.org/roi-calculator): Calculate Return on Investment (ROI), annualized ROI, and payback period. Free ROI calculator for marketing, business investments, and projects.
- [SAFE Note Equity Calculator](https://ratekit.org/safe-calculator): Calculate your SAFE note conversion, ownership percentage, and dilution. Supports valuation cap, discount rate. Free tool for founders and investors.
- [Salary to Hourly Calculator — Convert Annual Salary](https://ratekit.org/salary-hourly): Convert annual salary to hourly rate or hourly rate to annual salary. Accounts for work hours, paid time off, and holidays. Free salary converter.
- [Self-Employment Tax Calculator 2026](https://ratekit.org/self-employment-tax): Calculate US self-employment tax (15.3%), quarterly estimated payments, and how much to set aside from each paycheck. Free SE tax calculator for freelancers.
- [Stripe & PayPal Fee Calculator](https://ratekit.org/stripe-fee): Calculate exact Stripe and PayPal fees. Find out how much to charge your client to receive your desired amount after processing fees. Free, instant.
- [VAT & GST Calculator](https://ratekit.org/vat-calculator): Add or remove VAT and GST from any price. Supports all countries and custom rates. Free VAT calculator for invoicing and business.

## Russian Glossary (русский глоссарий)
Directory: [GET /ru/glossary](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary).
- [ROI (рентабельность инвестиций)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/roi): ROI показывает, сколько прибыли принесла инвестиция относительно её стоимости, в процентах.
- [Точка безубыточности](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/break-even-point): Точка безубыточности — это объём продаж (в единицах или выручке), при котором выручка равна всем затратам, а прибыль равна нулю.
- [Маржинальная прибыль (Contribution Margin)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/contribution-margin): Маржинальная прибыль — это выручка с одной единицы продажи за вычетом только переменных затрат на неё — сумма, которая «вносит вклад» в покрытие постоянных затрат и прибыли.
- [Наценка vs. Маржа](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/markup-vs-margin): Наценка — это прибыль в процентах от себестоимости; маржа — та же прибыль в процентах от цены продажи. Для одной и той же продажи это всегда разные числа.
- [Burn Rate (скорость сжигания денег)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/burn-rate): Burn rate — это сколько денег компания тратит в месяц, обычно делится на gross burn (общие расходы) и net burn (расходы минус выручка).
- [Runway стартапа](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/runway): Runway — это сколько месяцев компания может работать при текущем burn rate, прежде чем остаток денег обнулится.
- [CAC (стоимость привлечения клиента)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/cac): CAC — это полная стоимость продаж и маркетинга на привлечение одного нового клиента: общие затраты делятся на число привлечённых клиентов.
- [LTV (пожизненная ценность клиента)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/ltv): LTV — это общая валовая прибыль, которую бизнес ожидает получить от клиента за всё время, пока тот остаётся клиентом.
- [Соотношение LTV:CAC](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/ltv-cac-ratio): Соотношение LTV:CAC сравнивает, сколько стоит клиент (LTV), с тем, сколько стоит его привлечь (CAC); 3:1 — широко принятый ориентир здоровой экономики для SaaS.
- [SAFE (конвертируемый заём для стартапов)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/safe-note): SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) — инструмент привлечения инвестиций для стартапов, где инвестор даёт деньги сейчас в обмен на долю в компании при будущем раунде с оценкой, а не получает акции сразу.
- [Размытие доли (Dilution)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/equity-dilution): Размытие — это снижение процента владения существующего акционера, которое происходит, когда компания выпускает новые акции для новых инвесторов.
- [НДС / GST (налог на добавленную стоимость)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/vat-gst): НДС (или GST) — это налог на потребление, добавляемый на каждом этапе производства и собираемый продавцом, в конечном счёте его платит конечный потребитель.
- [Self-Employment Tax (налог на самозанятость в США)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/self-employment-tax): Американский self-employment tax — это налог 15,3% на социальное страхование и медицину, который платят фрилансеры и независимые подрядчики вместо налогов, которые обычно делит пополам работодатель.
- [FEIE (исключение иностранного трудового дохода)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/feie): FEIE позволяет гражданам США, живущим за рубежом и соответствующим требованиям, исключить установленную сумму иностранного дохода из федерального подоходного налога США каждый год.
- [APR (годовая процентная ставка)](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/apr): APR — это годовая стоимость заимствования денег в процентах, включающая и процентную ставку, и большинство разовых комиссий — правильное число для сравнения кредитов с разной структурой комиссий.
- [Амортизация кредита](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/amortization): Амортизация — это процесс погашения кредита равными периодическими платежами, где каждый платёж покрывает проценты за период плюс растущую долю основного долга.
- [EBITDA](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/ebitda): EBITDA (прибыль до вычета процентов, налогов, износа и амортизации) — показатель базовой операционной прибыльности компании, очищенный от финансовых и учётных решений.
- [Оплачиваемые и неоплачиваемые часы](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/billable-hours): Оплачиваемые часы — это время, за которое клиент платит напрямую; неоплачиваемые часы покрывают всё остальное, что фрилансер или агентство делает, чтобы бизнес работал.
- [Комиссии платёжных систем](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/payment-processing-fees): Платёжные системы вроде Stripe и PayPal берут процент плюс небольшую фиксированную комиссию с каждой карточной транзакции, что уменьшает сумму, которую реально получает продавец.
- [Прогноз денежного потока](https://ratekit.org/ru/glossary/cash-flow-forecast): Прогноз денежного потока показывает, сколько денег будет у бизнеса в будущие месяцы, исходя из ожидаемой выручки, затрат и стартового остатка на счету.
